chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) validated the testimony of women in debt, even if there was no man with them.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women's testimony in debt cases according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a specific nuance in Shia fiqh by validating women's testimony for debts even when no men are present, countering the view that male testimony is always required as a safeguard. It reflects the Prophet's (SAWW) practical application of the Quranic verse on debt, emphasizing sufficiency over redundancy in financial witnessing. This ruling underscores the reliability of women's testimony in commercial matters within the Shia legal tradition.
